children: Vitalist says its Reebok Kinetic smartwatch, its first commercial device built on VitalOS, is now available in Canada and the U.S. The company also extended the closing date of its up-to-C$10.0M private placements to Dec. 27, 2026; closing remains subject to conditions and approvals.
Reebok Kinetic now available in Canada and U.S.
The first commercial device built on VitalOS is on sale, providing an initial test of consumer demand; sales figures were not provided.
Private placement closing extended to Dec. 27
The financing remains incomplete, leaving execution and funding dependent on closing and required approvals.
Offerings total up to C$10.0M gross proceeds
The proposed financing could provide capital, but proceeds are not reported as raised and closing is not assured.
Debenture cap set at C$1.20; forced conversion removed
The revised terms change potential conversion pricing and eliminate the company's forced conversion option.

This is an early commercial milestone for VitalOS, alongside a previously announced financing that remains pending. Further evidence of product adoption or completed financing with final TSXV acceptance would make the developments more consequential.
